orderDelayDays.note: Runners at ~50-100 km/day over a 100-200 km theater, no staff system. Educated guess.
Runners and signal fires. Educated guess.
Roman relay posts: typical trip 38-62 miles (61-100 km) per day; over a ~100 km theater plus staff time ~1 day.
Mongol yam messengers covered 200-300 km/day via relay stations 20-40 miles apart; field armies without relays slower; mid 0.5.
Mounted couriers c.1600 (~cursus publicus speeds, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cursus_publicus) with larger armies. Educated guess.
Aides-de-camp on horseback; corps within a day's ride; semaphore for strategic messages only. Educated guess.
Telegraph/telephone to division, but orders for set-piece attacks took 12-24 h of staff work. Educated guess.
Radio down to company; division order cycle ~8-16 h. Educated guess.
Data links and satellite comms; brigade/division order cycle ~4-8 h. Educated guess.

Networked C4ISR; DCX-I networked CAS showed 'more than an order of magnitude' faster information sharing (https://www.afcea.org/signal-media/network-centric-warfare-offers-warfighting-advantage); staff cycle still bounds it. Educated guess.

coalitionFriction.note: Coordination penalty per extra member nation (slower order cycle, lower coordination). No quantitative source found. Educated guess.
